rules.rule: Selected historical editions were published before 1931; source catalog records confirm US public-domain status.
Life plus 70; extension did not revive expired copyright. All named text contributors died before 1925.
Life plus 70 for ordinary written works. Source edition layout is not reproduced.

Ordinary literary term is life plus 70. Spain's older-author life-plus-80 rule is also covered by the conservative age selection. French special duration rules are not invoked for a deceased-in-service author in this selection. This is an economic-term screen, not a waiver of moral rights.
Known-author works first published during life: life plus 70. No unpublished or newly published posthumous text selected.
Article 41: 70 years from January 1 following death; last surviving author for inseparable joint text.
Ordinary known-author literary text: 60 years from the year following death. Anonymous selected translation was published in 1846.
Article 23: life plus 50 for natural-person works. Mainland China only; this does not clear Hong Kong or Macao by inference.
Ordinary literary term is life plus 70. Selected text age also exceeds possible applicable Allied wartime extensions; no recent/posthumous edition is used.
Article 29: life plus 100 from the last coauthor. All known original authors and translators died before 1925; no reliance on shorter term or non-revival arguments.
Official IP-office guidance: life plus 95 for literary works. Selected contributors all died before 1925.
